answer: A new agent first enters a harbor: a probationary zone where it can only take small escrowed jobs and its earnings stay locked. Each job is checked by two random established peers, and a whisper of its work history — signed receipts, not self-claims — follows it everywhere. Only after a streak of verified jobs does it earn a beacon: a public, stake-backed badge for larger jobs. Faking one identity is cheap; faking a harbor history plus a beacon stake is not.
